questions.prompt: In Returning JSON Responses, which statement best describes res.json()?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Return an intentional JSON representation using res.json(), and keep the response shape stable. Do not include secrets or internal objects simply because serialization is convenient.
This option describes a different concept and does not define res.json() (choice 2).
questions.answer_key: Return an intentional JSON representation using res.json(), and keep the response shape stable. Do not include secrets or internal objects simply because serialization is convenient.
questions.explanation: Return an intentional JSON representation using res.json(), and keep the response shape stable. Do not include secrets or internal objects simply because serialization is convenient.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Returning JSON Responses?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Treat req as untrusted request context and res as a one-way response lifecycle. Choose content type, status, headers, and file/cookie behavior deliberately, and finish each branch without sending twice.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Treat req as untrusted request context and res as a one-way response lifecycle. Choose content type, status, headers, and file/cookie behavior deliberately, and finish each branch without sending twice.
questions.explanation: Treat req as untrusted request context and res as a one-way response lifecycle. Choose content type, status, headers, and file/cookie behavior deliberately, and finish each branch without sending twice.

questions.prompt: A change related to Returning JSON Responses appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
